newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks move higher in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks move higher in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks advanced smartly in early Friday trade on reduced but healthy turnover as some investors topped up long-term investment positions, brokers said.
"Today's trend is just a continuation of the firm trend we saw before Christmas," said Archie Hart, director, institutional sales at BZW Securities.
The Hang Seng was up 42 points to 13,384 after 45 minutes of trade and after touching an early high of 13,426.28. Turnover was a respectable HK$985 million.
Most of the activity was probably derived from local and U.S. based investors, since Thursday was also a holiday in the United Kingdom, said Hart.
Hang Seng Index futures showed fairly bullish trading patterns. The December contract was up 52 points to 13,492 and the January 85 points to 13,540.
The December contract will expire on Monday, December 30.
Properities led the market in early trade, followed by the finance sector, the market's leaders prior to the Christmas break, brokers said.
Only utilities declined in the first part of the session.
Cheung Kong led the property sector with a jump of HK$1.00 to HK$69.50. Sun Hung Kai Properties was up HK$0.50 at HK$95.50, while Henderson Land was unchanged at HK$75.75.
Index heavyweight HSBC Holdings advanced HK$1.50 to HK$164.50. The share's all time high was HK$168.50, also set on November 28.

Subsidiary Hang Seng Bank advanced HK$0.50 to HK$93.50.he property sector was led by Cheung Kong which put on a HK$1.00 to HK$69.50, Sun Hung Kai Properties was up HK$0.50 at HK$95.50, while Henderson Land was unchanged at HK$75.75.
Hongkong Telecom was unchanged at HK$12.65, and China Light at HK$33.50, while Hongkong Electric eased HK$0.10 to HK$25.85.

CITIC Pacific rose to a new all-time high in early Friday trade of HK$42.80, up HK$0.60. The previous all time high was HK$42.50, set on November 28. Brokers said trading in CITIC, which is the ninth largest listed company in terms of market capitalisation, was unlikely to be linked to index futures and stock options expiration on Monday.
Mid cap constituent and red chip China Resources added HK$0.55 to HK$15.05. The share touched its all time high of HK$15.20 in early trade.
Dah Sing Financial Holdings Ltd moved to a new high of HK$32.70, then fell back to trade HK$0.10 down at HK$31.90.
